In vitro, cigarette smoke extract (CSE) was used to induce injury in human bronchial epithelial (HBE) cells, followed by Rg1 treatment and ABCB1 overexpression or knockdown. Advanced glycation end products-receptor for advanced glycation end products (AGEs-RAGE) and early growth response protein 1-c-Jun N-terminal kinase (EGR1-JNK) signaling pathways were detected. In COPD rats, Rg1 markedly attenuated alveolar structural destruction and collagen deposition, decreased Ri, increased Cdyn and FEV0.3/FVC. ABCB1 knockdown partially reversed these protective effects. In HBE cells, Rg1 enhanced cell viability, restored mitochondrial membrane potential, reduced apoptosis, decreased ROS accumulation, and rescued intracellular ATP depletion. Rg1 inhibited the activation of the AGEs-RAGE and EGR1-JNK pathways in a manner associated with upregulation of ABCB1 expression. Ginsenoside Rg1 enhances mitochondrial function partially through upregulation of ABCB1 expression, thereby alleviating mitochondrial dysfunction in COPD rats and CSE-treated HBE cells.

title: Localized Chromatin Rewiring Shapes Rhythmic Transcription within a Stable 3D Genome in Rice
abstract: How spatial genome architecture coordinates rhythmic gene transcription across scales in plants remains poorly understood. Here, we integrated bridge linker Hi-C (BL-Hi-C), H3K9ac ChIP-seq and RNA-seq at six time points across a 24-h circadian cycle in rice. While global higher-order structure was largely invariant, with 84.5% of A/B compartments and over 95% of topologically associating domains (TADs) conserved across all time points, we identified 557 dynamic compartment transitions coupled to changes in active chromatin marks. Within this stable structural scaffold, 35.8% of TADs containing clustered loci of multiple rhythmic genes with synchronized expression phases. In contrast, fine-scale intradomain contacts and chromatin loops exhibited pronounced temporal plasticity. Chromatin interactions connected rhythmic genes with diverse expression phases. Myb-binding motifs were enriched at chromatin interaction anchors at dawn and early day (ZT0 and ZT4). Together, our findings demonstrate that localized chromatin rewiring occurs within relatively stable architectural frameworks, providing a spatiotemporal context for circadian gene regulation in rice.

title: Cd47 deficiency in mouse brain under excitotoxic stress.
abstract: CD47, a transmembrane protein with well-established immune and neurodevelopmental roles, was recently identified as an abundant presynaptic protein in humans, non-human primates, and mice. To investigate how Cd47 influences neuronal stress and injury, we performed single-nucleus RNA sequencing of hippocampi from wild-type (WT) and Cd47 knockout (KO) mice exposed to kainic acid (KA) at convulsive (KA25; 25 mg/kg) or subconvulsive (KA3; 3 mg/kg) doses. Integrating cell-type annotations with Weighted Gene Co-expression Network Analysis (WGCNA) revealed distinct neuronal and glial gene modules whose co-expression structure differed by genotype and by KA exposure. Notably, certain modules showed KA-associated changes in co-expression structure only in Cd47-deficient cells. Enrichment analyses of these modules highlighted translational, bioenergetic, and synaptic gene sets. Comparing transcriptome-wide distributions using Wasserstein distance demonstrated that vehicle-treated KO cells most closely resembled WT cells exposed to KA3, of all fifteen pairwise comparisons. These findings suggest that Cd47 loss shifts the hippocampal transcriptome toward a state resembling mild excitotoxic stress, implicating Cd47 as a candidate regulator of neuronal stress adaptation and providing a hypothesis for testing that role.

title: RPL22 suppresses tumor growth in undifferentiated/dedifferentiated endometrial carcinoma through IFIT3 downregulation.
abstract: Undifferentiated/dedifferentiated endometrial carcinoma (UDEC) represents a rare but aggressive subtype of endometrial cancer characterized by chemoresistance. Notably, a considerable proportion of patients with UDEC who exhibit mismatch repair deficiency respond favorably to immunotherapy. Here, we identified mutations in the ribosomal protein L22 (RPL22) gene in 42% (11/26) of UDEC samples - which occurred predominantly in mismatch repair-deficient tumors. Functionally, we demonstrated that RPL22 increased the sensitivity of UDEC cells to cisplatin and lenvatinib, while promoting T-cell-mediated cytotoxicity in the presence of combined lenvatinib and pembrolizumab. RNA sequencing revealed that RPL22 overexpression in UDEC cells downregulated interferon signaling pathways, including interferon-induced protein with tetratricopeptide repeats 3 (IFIT3). Further analyses supported a potential regulatory relationship between RPL22, IFIT3, and JAK/STAT1 signaling. In xenograft experiments, RPL22 overexpression reduced tumor growth, and concurrent IFIT3 overexpression attenuated this suppressive effect at the final time point. Collectively, these findings identify RPL22 as a potential regulator of drug sensitivity and immune responses in UDEC. We propose that the RPL22-IFIT3-JAK/STAT1 axis may offer opportunities for developing personalized therapeutic strategies in UDEC.

title: Nuclear NPR1 modulates salicylic acid/jasmonic acid crosstalk via transcriptional control of WRKY transcription factors.
abstract: NPR1 has a nuclear function in regulating salicylic acid/jasmonic acid crosstalk by activating specific WRKY transcription factors that suppress the jasmonic acid pathway, likely in part by reducing ORA59 accumulation. The plant hormones salicylic acid (SA) and jasmonic acid (JA) are major regulators of plant defense. They can antagonize each other's activity, enabling an optimized defense response. The SA master regulator NPR1 is a key player in this SA/JA crosstalk although the mechanisms of NPR1-mediated SA/JA crosstalk remain only partly understood, especially regarding the ethylene-coregulated ERF branch of the JA pathway. Here, we investigated the function of NPR1 in SA/JA crosstalk using several arabidopsis npr1 mutant variants. Assays using the NPR1-HBD and npr1-nls lines, expressing only cytosolic NPR1, revealed that NPR1 has a nuclear role in SA/JA crosstalk. RNA-seq analysis of lines expressing NPR1 mutated in residues Cys82 or Cys216, in which repression of the JA pathway was impaired while SA pathway induction remained mostly intact, identified 32 SA-responsive genes with reduced expression compared to Col-0, including four WRKY transcription factor genes. Of these, WRKY53 and WRKY70 could suppress expression of the JA marker gene PDF1.2 induced by ORA59, the master regulator of the ERF branch of the JA pathway, in a protoplast system. Additional SA-inducible WRKYs (WRKY50, WRKY54, WRKY63, and WRKY67) similarly suppressed ORA59-induced PDF1.2 expression, implicating WRKY63 and WRKY67 for the first time in SA/JA crosstalk and confirming earlier reports on the role of the other WRKY TFs. WRKY53 and WRKY67 were further shown to reduce accumulation of the ORA59 protein in protoplasts. Thus, our study indicated that NPR1 can regulate SA/JA crosstalk in the nucleus via transcriptional activation of genes encoding specific JA-repressing WRKY transcription factors.

title: Lgr5 deficiency accelerates intervertebral disc degeneration via NF-κB activation and enhanced osteoclastogenesis.
abstract: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IDD) is a common degenerative disease and the primary cause of low back pain. Leucine-rich repeat-containing G-protein coupled receptor 5 (Lgr5) is an activator of the canonical Wnt signaling pathway. But its role in IDD progression and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. Lgr5 knockout (Lgr5 KO) mice were generated by crossing Lgr5flox/flox mice with Prx1-Cre transgenic mice. These samples were analyzed by RNAseq, micro-CT, histology and western blotting, etc. MicroCT analysis of Lgr5 KO and wild-type (WT) mice caudal vertebrae showed that Lgr5 KO mice exhibited narrowed disc space, deteriorated trabecular bone microarchitecture, and decreased bone volume fraction (BV/TV). In a surgically induced IDD model, we showed that Lgr5 KO led to disrupted disc structure, nucleus pulposus (NP) atrophy, cellular loss, and decreased glycosaminoglycan content, thereby accelerating the progression of IDD. RNA-seq analysis identified 900 differentially expressed genes (457 upregulated, 443 downregulated) in Lgr5 KO discs, enriched in osteoclast differentiation, ECM-receptor interaction, and NF-κB signaling pathways. TRAP staining showed enhanced osteoclast activity in Lgr5 KO endplates. Western blot demonstrated reduced Collagen II and increased MMP13, p-p65 in Lgr5 KO NP cells. Immunofluorescence and immunohistochemical staining confirmed that Lgr5 deficiency increased MMP13, p-p65, and Active caspase-3, while decreasing PCNA, promoting inflammation, apoptosis, and suppressing proliferation in NP cells. Collectively, our results demonstrated that Lgr5 deficiency increased inflammation, disrupted ECM homeostasis and NP cell functions, which finally accelerated IDD.

title: Postmenopausal estradiol levels and female sex modulate haemodynamic responsiveness in experimental portal hypertension.
abstract: Sex and 17β-estradiol (E2) influence outcomes of cirrhosis, yet preclinical studies in portal hypertension are conducted predominantly in males. We investigated sex and E2-dependent differences in G protein-coupled estrogen receptor 1 (GPER1) signalling and portal pressure response to PDE5 inhibition (PDE5i) in experimental cirrhosis. We assessed sex inclusion in rodent studies by PubMed literature search and analysed human hepatic GPER1 expression by sex and age using bulk RNA-seq. Bile duct ligation was performed in male, ovariectomised (OVX) and sham-operated female rats. E2 was administered 24h before invasive haemodynamic assessment in males and OVX females. Acute PDE5i effects were investigated during haemodynamic measurement. Of 510 rat and 1,657 mouse studies, 87.3% and 77.3% respectively included males only. Human bulk RNA-seq suggested lower hepatic GPER1 expression in cirrhotic females aged ≥ 50 vs. < 50 years. OVX reduced hepatic - but not aortic - GPER1 expression. E2 reduced portal pressure (mean +/- SEM; 22.6 +/- 1.4 vs. 14.3 +/- 1.1 mmHg, p = 0.009) by lowering hepatic portal vascular resistance (74.4 ± 12.7 vs. 25.4 +/- 3.1 mmHg·min·ml-1·g-1, p = 0.03) only in OVX females. PDE5i decreased portal pressure in males (21.3 +/- 1.2 vs. 16.9 +/- 1.8 mmHg, p = 0.03) irrespective of E2. OVX abolished the PDE5i response, which was restored by E2 (14.3 +/- 1.1 vs. 10.0 +/- 0.9 mmHg, p = 0.04). In experimental cirrhosis, estradiol depletion in OVX females was associated with reduced hepatic GPER1 expression and a diminished portal pressure response to PDE5i. This highlights sex and menopausal status as key determinants of treatment response in portal hypertension and supports the need for sex-specific validation. Sex and hormonal status likely contribute to clinically relevant variability in the pharmacology of portal hypertension. Our work highlights that haemodynamic drug response varies due to sex and estradiol status in pre- and postmenopausal females, yet preclinical studies predominantly rely on male models. Integrating sex and menopausal status into early drug development could improve translational accuracy and anticipate non-responder populations.

title: Exonuclease-gated CRISPR/Cas12a biosensing strategy for sensitive detection of lncRNA MIR155HG.
abstract: Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) have been shown to be important regulatory factors in initiation and progression of cancer. However, sensitive detection of lncRNAs remains challenging due to their low abundance, complex structure and susceptibility to nuclease degradation. Among various lncRNAs, MIR155HG has been shown to be involved in the progression of cervical cancer and serve as a potential target for biomarker analysis. Here, we developed an exonuclease-gated CRISPR/Cas12a biosensing platform (E-CRISPR) for the detection of MIR155HG without target pre-amplification. This strategy relies on a bifunctional single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) probe containing both a MIR155HG recognition region and a CRISPR/Cas12a activation region. In the absence of target RNA, exonuclease I (Exo I) degrades the ssDNA probe, thereby reducing background signals. Upon binding to MIR155HG, RNA-DNA hybridization reduces the probe's susceptibility to Exo I digestion and allows the retained probe to activate CRISPR/Cas12a and generate an enhanced fluorescence signal. Under optimized conditions, the E-CRISPR assay achieved a limit of detection of 4.76 pM and a linear range of 4.76 pM to 0.4 nM. The entire assay could be completed within 100 min while maintaining sensitive detection of MIR155HG and showed good sequence specificity and reliable performance in complex biological environment. This exonuclease-regulated CRISPR/Cas12a strategy provides a simple analytical approach for extracellular lncRNA analysis.

title: Nitrogen-source responses of Spirogyra across defined media and authentic wastewater: Control-aware process accounting, ¹⁵N tracing, and transcriptomics.
abstract: The percentage-removal metric cannot distinguish algal nutrient capture from abiotic loss or ensure that performance in a defined medium transfer to authentic wastewater. We addressed both limitations for the filamentous green alga Spirogyra sp. FACHB-1990 using a control-aware process inventory, ¹⁵N tracing, and time-matched transcriptomics. In a defined municipal-wastewater medium, NH₄⁺-N and NO₃⁻-N declined by 53% and 84%, respectively, over 96 h. A nitrogen inventory closing at 93.7% recovery attributed only approximately 38% of the filtered TDN decline to biomass N. Recovery-corrected NH₃ trapping accounted for approximately 16% of apparent ammonium loss, and a pH-trajectory-approximated algae-free control lost 46.5% of filtered TDP. Against a batch-matched synthetic reference, one authentic primary-effluent batch yielded 96 h TN transfer coefficients of 0.758 unfiltered (95% CI 0.616-0.896) and 0.921 following 0.22 µm filtration (0.762-1.097). Parallel ¹⁵N tracing at equal 13.5 mg N L⁻¹ pools gave excess-¹⁵N biomass-inventory ratios of 18.69 at 6 h (15.02-23.41) and 5.78 at 72 h (4.56-7.23). The labeled pools were designed to be nominally near-matched at approximately 10 atom %, but substrate-pool enrichment was not assayed. These ratios are therefore semi-quantitative cumulative contrasts rather than fluxes. Time-matched RNA-seq showed lower NRT2.1 abundance under NH₄⁺ than NO₃⁻ at 6 h (log₂FC = -3.90). Percentage-removal figures for filamentous-algae systems therefore require a closed nutrient inventory and an authentic-wastewater benchmark before they can inform process design.

title: BAHCC1 Drives Smooth Muscle Plasticity and Neointima via Epigenetic Repression.
abstract: Vascular smooth muscle cell (SMC) phenotypic plasticity drives neointimal hyperplasia (IH) and contributes to atherosclerosis. Epigenetic mechanisms have been implicated in SMC plasticity, but the roles of epigenetic reader proteins are poorly understood. BAHCC1 (bromo adjacent homology domain coiled-coil 1) is a newly identified reader of the gene-repression histone mark histone-3 lysine 27 trimethylation (H3K27me3). Its role in vascular remodeling is unknown. We investigated BAHCC1 in human restenotic and atherosclerotic arteries and in rat and mouse arterial injury models using BAHCC1 silencing, SMC-specific deletion, and an H3K27me3-binding-deficient knock-in mutation. Mechanistic studies in human aortic SMCs integrated transcriptomic and epigenomic profiling, protein-interaction assays, and single-guide RNA-dCas9-based epigenetic editing. BAHCC1 was upregulated in human restenotic and atherosclerotic arteries and rat arteries with IH. While BAHCC1 silenc ing reduced IH in balloon-injured rat arteries, SMC-specific BAHCC1 deletion and the H3K27me3-binding-deficient mutation (BAHCC1Y2537A) attenuated IH in wire-injured mouse arteries. In human SMCs, mitogen induced BAHCC1 expression through nuclear factor Y subunit-α, promoting BAHCC1-dependent dedifferentiation. Integrated transcriptomics and epigenomics identified LMO7 (LIM domain only 7), an IH suppressor, as a key BAHCC1-repressed target. BAHCC1 occupancy at LMO7 required BAHCC1-H3K27me3 interaction, and LMO7-targeted H3K27me3 enrichment through epigenetic editing repressed its expression in a BAHCC1-dependent manner. Furthermore, BAHCC1 associated with SAP30 and RBBP4/7 to form a corepressor complex. Functionally, LMO7 silencing reversed the effects of BAHCC1 knockdown on human SMC phenotype and exacerbated IH in BAHCC1Y2537A mice. Human genetic analyses further identified BAHCC1 variants associated with cardiovascular phenotypes and BAHCC1 expression. BAHCC1 is a previously unrecognized epigenetic driver of vascular remodeling. By reading H3K27me3 and recruiting corepressors to repress gene expression, BAHCC1 promotes pathological SMC phenotypic transition and IH, highlighting the BAHCC1 pathway as a potential therapeutic target for IH-associated vascular disease.

title: Genetic variants shape single-cell chromatin accessibility and disease risk.
abstract: Understanding how genetic variation shapes gene regulation at single-cell resolution is crucial for elucidating complex disease mechanisms1, but has been limited by the lack of large-scale single-cell multi-omics data2-4. Here we present single-cell assay for transposase-accessible chromatin with sequencing of 3.5 million peripheral blood mononuclear cells from 1,042 donors with matched whole-genome sequencing. Across 28 immune cell types, we tested 440,996 chromatin accessibility peaks and identified 243,225 chromatin accessibility quantitative trait loci (caQTLs) at 100,483 peaks, 60% of them cell-type specific. Rare variant analysis identified 38,161 associated peaks, with predicted transcription factor-binding disruption implicated at individual loci. Colocalization with expression QTLs (eQTLs) from single-cell RNA sequencing data (5.4 million peripheral blood mononuclear cells)5 defined 28,834 candidate cis-regulatory elements. Across genome-wide association studies for 16 diseases and 44 blood traits, caQTLs colocalized 4.5-22.6% more signals than eQTLs alone. Cell-type-specific and tissue-specific context, distal effects and multi-causal-variant models raised genome-wide association study-eQTL concordance from approximately 16% to approximately 65%. Cell state further modulates genetic effects, with 27% of over 200,000 caQTL-cell-state interactions lacking a main effect. At the inflammatory bowel disease risk gene ADCY7, accessibility effects varied with genotype and G protein-mediated pathway activity in CD4+ T cells. A graph neural network trained on both eQTL and caQTL layers inferred peak-gene links in unpaired multiome data with up to 17.2% higher accuracy than QTL-agnostic data, uncovering 128 additional transcription factor-target pairs (22% increase). Together, these results show that genetic variants shape chromatin accessibility in a cell-type-specific and cell-state-specific manner, influencing immune function and disease risk.

title: Targeting DDX6 attenuates osteoarthritis progression by inhibiting CPEB1-mediated ferroptosis in subchondral bone.
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a prevalent degenerative joint disorder characterized by the deterioration of articular cartilage, leading to pain and joint stiffness. Ferroptosis is involved in the progression of OA and plays a pivotal role in its pathogenesis. The study aimed to investigate the mechanism by which DEAD-box helicase 6 (DDX6) regulates ferroptosis by interacting with cytoplasmic polyadenylation element-binding protein 1 (CPEB1) and contributes to OA progression by regulating osteosclerosis and microangiogenesis. Ferroptosis in the subchondral bone and the interaction between DDX6 and CPEB1 in OA osteoblasts were examined in vitro. Expression levels of proteins associated with ferroptosis, osteosclerosis, and H-type microangiogenesis were measured following DDX6 and CPEB1 overexpression or knockdown using lentiviral and small-interfering RNA transfection. In vivo, we used 10-week-old mice with osteoblast-specific conditional knockout of Ddx6 (Ddx6fl/fl OC-Cre+) and intra-articular injection of ferrostatin-1 in a destabilization of the medial meniscus-induced OA model to evaluate effects on cartilage degeneration, microangiogenic activity, and subchondral bone microarchitecture. Ferroptosis in OA osteoblasts, driven by mitochondrial dysfunction and the DDX6-CPEB1 interaction, was confirmed. Both DDX6 and CPEB1 were upregulated in subchondral bone of patients with OA and model mice. Upregulation or downregulation of DDX6 and CPEB1 levels led to corresponding changes in the expression of downstream H-type microangiogenesis-related proteins (vascular endothelial growth factor, hypoxia-inducible factor 1 alpha, cluster of differentiation 31, and endomucin), bone osteosclerosis-related proteins (osteocalcin [OCN], runt-related transcription factor 2 [RUNX2] and glutathione peroxidase 4 [GPX4]). These alterations ultimately affected chondrocyte metabolism through the bone-cartilage functional unit. Conditional knockout of Ddx6 reduced subchondral microvascular infiltration and alleviated cartilage destruction, whereas intra-articular ferrostatin-1 injection showed even greater protective effects. DDX6 promotes OA progression by regulating ferroptosis through interaction with CPEB1, which in turn influences H-type microangiogenesis and osteosclerosis. Targeting DDX6 may represent a promising therapeutic strategy for OA.

title: RNA binding motif protein 15 (RBM15) inhibits macrophage phagocytosis via m6A-dependent colony stimulating factor 2 (CSF2)/STAT3 pathway in pancreatic cancer.
abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains a major public health challenge worldwide, marked by difficulties in early diagnosis and a dismal prognosis. The overtly immunosuppressive nature of its tumor microenvironment (TME) renders PDAC largely refractory to existing immunotherapies. Tumor-associated macrophages, the predominant immune infiltrate in the TME, are pivotal in facilitating immune escape. While m6A RNA methylation, the most abundant eukaryotic post-transcriptional modification, is known to contribute to PDAC progression, its specific function in mediating tumor-immune interactions has yet to be fully elucidated. We identify RBM15, a core m6A methyltransferase component, as a key regulator of macrophage phagocytosis in PDAC. RBM15 is notably upregulated in PDAC tissues and is associated with immunosuppressive macrophage infiltration and poor prognosis. Mechanistically, RBM15 binds CSF2 mRNA and enhances its stability in an m6A-dependent manner, thereby increasing CSF2 secretion from pancreatic cancer cells. Tumor-derived CSF2 then activates STAT3 signaling in macrophages, thereby impairing their phagocytic function. In vivo orthotopic models further demonstrate that RBM15 promotes PDAC progression and is accompanied by activation of the CSF2/STAT3 axis and increased immunosuppressive macrophage infiltration. Collectively, our findings reveal a novel non-cell-autonomous mechanism whereby tumor cell m6A modification regulates macrophage function, and provide experimental evidence supporting a potential role of the RBM15/CSF2/STAT3 axis in the immunosuppressive remodeling of the PDAC microenvironment.

title: Deep Lineage: Single-cell lineage tracing and fate inference using deep learning.
abstract: Recent advances in single-cell RNA sequencing and lineage tracing techniques have provided valuable insights into the temporal changes in gene expression during development, tumor progression, and disease onset. However, there are few computational methods available to analyze this information to help understand multicellular dynamics. We introduce Deep Lineage, a deep-learning method for analyzing time-series single-cell RNA sequencing with matched lineage tracing data. Our method accurately predicts early cell fate biases and gene expression profiles at different time points within a clone, surpassing existing methods in fate prediction accuracy. We further validate our model using LineageSim, a fate-aware lineage simulator, demonstrating robustness to technical noise such as barcode dropout and clone misidentification. Additionally, we apply Deep Lineage to in silico perturbations in cellular reprogramming and hematopoiesis to identify key genes and pathways associated with cell fate determination and propose testable perturbation hypotheses for experimental follow-up.

title: TRMT112 Expression Is Associated With Poor Prognosis and Increased Invasive Potential in Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
abstract: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) has a poor prognosis and is frequently diagnosed at advanced stages. Therefore, the identification of clinically useful tumor biomarkers is a critical unmet need. The tRNA methyltransferase subunit 11-2 (TRMT112) forms a complex with methyltransferase-like protein 5 (METTL5) and is involved in RNA methylation; however, limited evidence suggests a role for TRMT112 as a tumor-promoting factor in cancer. Therefore, the biological function of TRMT112 in cancer, including OSCC, remains largely unknown, prompting this study. Analyses of public databases revealed that TRMT112 expression was associated with poor prognosis in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma and was positively correlated with METTL5 expression levels. TRMT112 was also associated with increased sensitivity to osimertinib and lestaurtinib. Furthermore, RNA polymerase II subunit G (POLR2G) and Sjögren's syndrome/scleroderma autoantigen 1 (SSSCA1, also termed ZNRD2) were identified as newly related genes. Immunohistochemical staining revealed that the TRMT112 protein was associated with an invasive growth pattern (p = 0.0234) and poorer prognosis (p = 0.0205). Functional assays indicated that TRMT112 was associated with increased invasive potential and regulation of METTL5 expression in OSCC cells. These findings suggest that TRMT112 may serve as a potential diagnostic and therapeutic target in OSCC.

title: Emodin attenuates CFA-induced inflammatory pain in association with suppression of the Cx3cl1/Cx3cr1/p38 MAPK signaling axis.
abstract: To investigate the analgesic effect of emodin on Complete Freund's Adjuvant (CFA)-induced inflammatory pain and to clarify the underlying molecular mechanism. Emodin was administered intraperitoneally or prophylactically to attenuate CFA-induced inflammatory pain. RNA-seq was performed to identify the biological functions of differentially expressed genes in mouse dorsal root ganglion (DRG) tissues. The expression levels of Cx3cl1/Cx3cr1 were evaluated by RT-qPCR, Western blotting, and immunofluorescence. Pharmacological and genetic approaches were employed to block Cx3cr1 and assess its effect on pain thresholds in CFA-treated mice. Hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining was used to examine the infiltration of immune and inflammatory cells in dorsal root ganglion (DRG) tissues before and after emodin treatment. Following emodin treatment, the levels of p-p38/p38 in DRG tissues were determined by Western blotting, and the mRNA levels of the pro-inflammatory cytokines Tnf-α, Il-1β, and Il-6 in DRG tissues were measured by RT-qPCR. Both therapeutic and prophylactic administration of emodin effectively alleviated CFA-induced mechanical and thermal hypersensitivity. Emodin treatment suppressed the CFA-induced upregulation of Cx3cl1/Cx3cr1 mRNA and protein levels in the DRG. Pharmacological and genetic blockade of Cx3cr1 effectively attenuated CFA-induced hyperalgesia. In addition, emodin markedly inhibited p-p38/p38 protein expression in the DRG of mice with CFA-induced inflammatory pain, reduced immune cell infiltration in DRG tissues, and downregulated the levels of the pro-inflammatory cytokines Tnf-α, Il-1β, and Il-6. Emodin attenuated CFA-induced inflammatory pain in mice, an effect associated with reduced Cx3cl1/Cx3cr1 signaling, decreased p38 MAPK activation, diminished immune-cell infiltration in the DRG, and lower expression of the proinflammatory cytokines Tnf-α, Il-1β, and Il-6 in DRG tissue.

title: ARTP Mutagenesis and Omics-Guided Target Validation for Improved Human Serum Albumin Fusion Protein Production in Yeast.
abstract: Efficient production of human serum albumin (HSA) fusion proteins in yeast remains constrained by the combined demands of folding, secretion, and cellular resource allocation. Rational optimization of endoplasmic reticulum folding and unfolded protein response pathways can improve production, but additional cellular constraints may persist in engineered strains. Here, we combined iterative atmospheric and room-temperature plasma (ARTP) mutagenesis, activity-coupled screening, and genome- and transcriptome-guided validation to improve production of an amylase-HSA fusion protein (AGSH) in Saccharomyces cerevisiae. Using extracellular α-amylase activity as the screening indicator, five rounds of ARTP mutagenesis in the folding-optimized strain AH28 generated mutants with enhanced AGSH production. The final mutant N5S14 reached 2.12-fold the AH28 level in AGSH-associated α-amylase activity. Physiological profiling showed that enhanced production was associated with altered growth-production balance and changes in glucose, ethanol, and glycerol profiles. Whole-genome sequencing identified 33 candidate mutation sites, and reverse engineering validated genes associated with improved AGSH production, including BUD27, NPR3, NPR2, and IML1. RNA-seq revealed distinct transcriptional states involving central carbon metabolism, protein folding, and stress-related processes. Transcriptome-guided validation identified PFY1 deletion and SSA3 overexpression as additional beneficial interventions. Overall, this strategy improved AGSH production and identified engineering targets beyond previously optimized folding-related modules.

title: MXene-Protein Corona Interfaces for Molecular Profiling of Alzheimer's Disease.
abstract: The protein corona (PC) that forms on the surface of nanomaterials upon contact with biological fluids provides a molecular snapshot of the host's physiological and pathological state. Here, we investigate two-dimensional (2D) titanium carbide (Ti3C2Tx) MXene nanosheets as nanobiointerfaces for capturing Alzheimer's disease (AD)-associated plasma protein signatures. Ti3C2Tx MXene flakes were incubated with plasma from clinically diagnosed AD patients and age-matched healthy controls (HC), leading to the formation of Ti3C2Tx MXene-PC complexes. Physicochemical characterization using dynamic light scattering, zeta potential analysis, and transmission electron microscopy revealed disease-dependent changes in hydrodynamic size, surface charge, and PC profile. Proteomic analysis of the isolated PC layers quantified 1,611 proteins without prior fractionation, demonstrating broad plasma proteome coverage. Principal component analysis (PCA) revealed disease-associated separation between AD and HC-derived Ti3C2Tx MXene PC proteomes along specific principal components despite interindividual heterogeneity. Differential abundance analysis identified selective enrichment of heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoproteins (hnRNPs), annexins, and inflammatory mediators in AD-derived PC, implicating dysregulated RNA metabolism, membrane stress responses, and immune activation, hallmark processes in AD pathology. Our findings demonstrate that Ti3C2Tx MXene-PC interfaces reshape the detectable plasma proteome and enable disease-associated molecular phenotyping, establishing a versatile nanointerface-driven framework for AD-related proteomic fingerprinting and molecular profiling. These results provide a foundation for future studies exploring MXene-based biointerfaces for plasma biomarker discovery and translational diagnostic applications.

title: Functional consequences of acanthocephalan infection in Homarus americanus and advances in understanding of parasite-associated changes in lobster immunity.
abstract: Profilicollis botulus is an acanthocephalan parasite with larval stages developing in arthropod intermediate hosts and adult stages maturing in vertebrate definitive hosts, typically seabirds. Despite its widespread occurrence in coastal ecosystems, the physiological and molecular consequences of P. botulus infection in the American lobster (Homarus americanus) remain unclear. In this exploratory observational study, we combined whole-animal respirometry with hepatopancreas RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) to characterize physiological and transcriptional differences between naturally infected and uninfected lobsters. Infected lobsters exhibited significantly lower mass-specific oxygen consumption than uninfected individuals (28.51 ± 1.87 vs 35.02 ± 1.49 mg O₂ kg-1 h-1). Exploratory transcriptomic analysis of a limited number of individuals (four infected and three uninfected) identified 324 differentially expressed genes (FDR < 0.05), including 232 downregulated and 92 upregulated transcripts in infected lobsters. Several transcripts associated with glycolysis and related metabolic processes showed higher expression in infected individuals. Conversely, lower transcript abundance was observed for multiple genes associated with innate immune functions, including lectin-type pattern recognition receptors, antimicrobial peptides (including anti-lipopolysaccharide factors), and components of the prophenoloxidase and coagulation systems, antioxidant enzymes, acute-phase proteins, and crustacean hyperglycemic hormone. Together, these findings associate reduced aerobic metabolism with lower expression of multiple innate immune-related transcripts in the hepatopancreas, a pattern that may be compatible with a stabilized host-parasite interaction and altered energetic allocation during parasitism. However, given the observational design and limited transcriptomic sample size, these interpretations remain hypotheses rather than demonstrated mechanisms. Together with other studies of parasite infections in crustaceans, our findings suggest that host responses to acanthocephalan infection may be host-dependent and influenced by parasite biology, tissue specificity, and host physiological condition. Further studies incorporating larger sample sizes, controlled infection experiments, and functional measurements are needed to determine whether these associations reflect direct effects of infection or other host-related and environmental factors.

title: Transcriptomic analysis identifies candidate genes associated with striated muscle contraction during breast muscle development in meat-type ducks.
abstract: The development of the breast muscle is critical for meat yield and quality in meat-type ducks. However, the transcriptional changes underlying breast muscle development in meat-type ducks remain poorly understood. In this study, we integrated phenotypic, histological, and myogenic regulatory factor analyses to characterize the developmental trajectory of the breast muscle, identifying embryonic day 19 (E19) as a pivotal transition point marked by peak muscle growth rate and maximal expression of MYOD, MYOG, and MYF5. Consequently, transcriptomic profiling of the pectoralis major muscle was conducted at three representative developmental stages, embryonic day 11 (E11), E19, and day of hatching (D1) using 15 cDNA libraries for RNA sequencing (RNA-seq). Pairwise comparisons identified 5,300, 5,167, and 8,393 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in the E11 vs. E19, E19 vs. D1, and E11 vs. D1 comparisons, respectively. These DEGs were subsequently subjected to Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analyses. Following the identification of common DEGs across the three developmental stages, protein-protein interaction (PPI) network analysis was integrated with gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA). This analysis revealed 24 common key genes involved in breast muscle development during meat-type duck growth, which converged our investigation specifically on the striated muscle contraction gene set. Furthermore, by integrating CytoHubba ranking and GSEA, we identified a core set of six candidate genes associated with striated muscle contraction during breast muscle development in ducks, namely ACTN2, MYH11, MYL1, TNNC1, TNNI1, and TNNI2. In conclusion, our findings delineate the dynamic transcriptomic landscape of duck breast muscle development and identify candidate genes associated with striated muscle contraction, which would be useful for future functional investigations of these genes and for developing molecular markers in ducks.

title: Microglia-targeted delivery of MCC950 suppresses NLRP3-IL-18-mediated neuroinflammation and retinal injury in retinal vein occlusion.
abstract: Retinal vein occlusion (RVO) causes retinal ischemia, macular edema, and vision loss, yet current anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) therapies primarily limit vascular leakage and leave ischemia-driven neuroinflammation insufficiently controlled. Here, we reveal a critical role for microglia-associated NLRP3-IL-18 signaling in amplifying inflammation during early RVO. Bulk retinal RNA sequencing showed broad innate immune activation, whereas single-cell transcriptomic profiling and spatial protein analysis identified prominent inflammasome-related changes in retinal microglia. Constitutive global deletion of Nlrp3 or Il18 attenuated microglial activation and preserved retinal structure and electrophysiological function. To translate this mechanistic insight into a targeted anti-inflammatory strategy, we engineered MG1-functionalized, MCC950-loaded nanoliposomes for microglia-targeted NLRP3 inhibition. MG1 functionalization promoted preferential nanoparticle uptake by activated microglia and suppressed NLRP3-IL-18 signaling more effectively than free MCC950 or non-targeted nanoliposomes. In experimental RVO, a single intravitreal dose administered 6 h after induction alleviated retinal inflammation and edema while preserving retinal electrophysiological responses. These findings establish microglia-associated NLRP3-IL-18 signaling as a therapeutic target in early RVO and support MG1-MCC950 nanoliposomes as a bioactive nanotherapeutic platform for RVO.

title: Molecular Adaptations and Sex-Biased Regulatory Pathways in Multi-Year Diapause of the Cabbage Beetle Colaphellus bowringi: A Duration-Resolved Transcriptomic Analysis.
abstract: The cabbage beetle Colaphellus bowringi, a key pest of cruciferous crops, exhibits a multiyear dormancy strategy characterized by pronounced interindividual variation in diapause duration: individuals entering summer or winter diapause-though initiated synchronously within each seasonal cohort-may remain in diapause for periods ranging from several months to as long as 5 years. To elucidate the molecular underpinnings of this extended dormancy and its sex-specific regulatory patterns, we performed a duration-resolved, sex-stratified transcriptomic analysis. Adult males and females were sampled after 0.5, 1, and 2 years of diapause durations and subjected to high-throughput RNA sequencing. De novo assembly yielded 66,379 unigenes, of which 16,132 (24.3%) were removed as non-arthropod contamination, leaving 50,247 unigenes that were used for all downstream annotation and expression analyses. Comparative transcriptomic profiling revealed a conserved adaptive strategy during prolonged diapause: patterns consistent with coordinated suppression of energy-intensive metabolic processes coupled with increased transcript abundance of genes in cellular protection pathways-including antioxidant defense, xenobiotic detoxification, and protein homeostasis mechanisms. Sex-biased transcriptional responses were observed: females showed comparable or higher numbers of differentially expressed genes in matched duration comparisons, with sustained transcript abundance of genes associated with reproductive processes and somatic maintenance, whereas males displayed greater duration-dependent transcriptional remodeling, particularly in signaling cascades and physiological homeostasis networks. KEGG pathway enrichment analysis identified sustained activation of glutathione metabolism, autophagy, and lysosomal degradation pathways throughout diapause; notably, extended diapause (2 years) was specifically associated with significant enrichment of immune response and lipid metabolism pathways. Duration-dependent dynamics in gene expression underscore that diapause is not a static quiescent state but a highly regulated, multi-stage process involving duration-specific transcriptional reconfiguration. This study establishes the first duration-resolved, sex-resolved transcriptomic resource for C. bowringi and advances mechanistic understanding of long-term insect diapause-thereby informing the development of targeted, environmentally sustainable pest management strategies.

title: An ARG1-associated immunometabolic program in bone marrow PMN-MDSC-like cells in multiple sclerosis and experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis.
abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic inflammatory demyelinating disease of the central nervous system. Recent work indicates that bone-marrow hematopoietic niches sense CNS autoimmunity and enhance myeloid output. However, whether MS bone marrow contains an immunometabolic PMN-MDSC-like state, and whether related ARG1-associated observations can be examined in a cross-species EAE context, remains unclear. We reanalyzed single-cell RNA sequencing data from treatment-naive patients with MS and healthy controls, focusing on myeloid states. We used donor-aware proportion analysis, trajectory inference, module scoring, donor-pseudobulk pathway enrichment, expression-based transcription-factor prioritization, co-expression analysis, ligand-target inference, and ARG1 virtual perturbation. We also quantified flow-gated bone marrow PMN-MDSCs and ARG1 protein in MOG35-55-induced EAE and tested systemic prophylactic oral nor-NOHA. MS bone marrow showed myeloid skewing and a heterogeneous PMN-MDSC-like transcriptional state, while donor-level subtype proportions were comparable between groups. Neutrophil degranulation showed the strongest BH-supported donor-pseudobulk enrichment, and expression-based regulatory and communication analyses converged on an ARG1-associated network. In EAE, flow-gated bone-marrow PMN-MDSCs and ARG1 protein were increased, and systemic prophylactic nor-NOHA was associated with lower clinical scores and reduced spinal-cord pathology. These data identify an ARG1-associated immunometabolic program in bone-marrow PMN-MDSC-like cells and connect the human transcriptional landscape with ARG1 protein expression and pharmacologic responses in EAE. Together, the findings establish ARG1-associated immunometabolism as a focused pathway for mechanistic and translational investigation.

title: Topology-adjusted knockout (TAKO): interpretable in silico single-gene knockout ranking on wild-type single-cell gene regulatory networks.
abstract: Predicting single-gene knockout effects from wild-type single-cell RNA-seq data remains challenging when perturbation experiments are costly and existing approaches require knockout-specific model training. Here we introduce Topology-Adjusted Knockout (TAKO), a computationally efficient WT-only framework for single-gene KO impact ranking on single-cell gene regulatory networks. The method applies a strict cut-in-and-out intervention on network transition dynamics and quantifies impact by contrasting stationary propagation profiles before and after perturbation under the same restart distribution. In SERGIO simulations, TAKO recovered direct regulator-target structure but did not show a consistent global advantage over a matched absolute Pearson-correlation ranking across network sizes. Direct evaluation against measured responses in Trem2 and Nkx2-1 KO data likewise yielded mixed global discrimination, although TAKO contained more differentially expressed genes among the top-ranked candidates in both examples. These results position TAKO as a fast, interpretable topology-based prioritisation method rather than a generally superior predictor of post-KO expression responses.

title: GOLM1 interacts with EGFR and contributes to increased intestinal permeability in ulcerative colitis through p38 MAPK signaling.
abstract: Golgi membrane protein 1 (GOLM1) has been implicated in inflammatory and fibrotic processes, yet its role in ulcerative colitis (UC) remains unclear. This study aimed to systematically evaluate the expression of GOLM1 in intestinal mucosal tissues and peripheral blood of UC patients, analyze its correlation with clinicopathological features, and investigate its regulatory effect on intestinal mucosal barrier function along with the underlying molecular mechanisms. Colonic mucosal biopsy specimens and peripheral blood samples were collected from patients with UC (including active and inactive disease) and healthy controls. GOLM1 expression in tissues was assessed via RNA sequencing, immunohistochemistry, western blotting, and quantitative real-time PCR (qPCR), while serum GOLM1 levels were measured by ELISA. Using a dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced mouse colitis model and an LPS-stimulated inflammatory model in NCM460 intestinal epithelial cells, GOLM1 was knocked down in vivo, and both knocked down and overexpressed in vitro, to evaluate its effects on intestinal permeability, tight junction protein expression, and downstream signaling pathways. GOLM1 expression was elevated in colonic tissues and serum from patients with UC compared with healthy controls. Serum GOLM1 concentrations were associated with clinical disease activity and inflammatory or immune-related markers. Protein interaction assays supported an association between GOLM1 and EGFR. Genetic gain- and loss-of-function experiments implicated EGFR and p38 MAPK signaling in GOLM1-associated alterations in tight junction protein expression and epithelial barrier readouts. In a DSS-induced mouse model of colitis, GOLM1 knockdown alleviated colonic inflammation and improved intestinal barrier function. GOLM1 interacts with EGFR and promotes intestinal inflammation and epithelial barrier dysfunction in UC through the p38 MAPK signaling pathway. These findings provide new insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying GOLM1-mediated intestinal injury in UC and lay the foundation for further mechanistic investigations.

title: SMAD family member 9 restrains MYC-associated zinc finger protein-driven Wnt family member 7A transcription in endometrial carcinoma.
abstract: Endometrial carcinoma (EC) is a common gynecological malignancy with increasing incidence and limited treatment options for advanced disease. The molecular mechanisms underlying its progression remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify SMAD family member 9 (SMAD9, also known as SMAD8) as a negative regulator of EC progression. Integrated analyses of clinical datasets and patient samples showed that SMAD9 is consistently downregulated in EC, and higher SMAD9 expression is associated with a more favorable prognosis. Functional assays showed that SMAD9 suppresses EC cell proliferation and cell-cycle progression, whereas its silencing enhances these phenotypes. Mechanistically, DNMT3B-mediated promoter hypermethylation contributes to reduced SMAD9 expression in EC. RNA sequencing and subsequent validation identified WNT7A as a downstream target of SMAD9. SMAD9 represses WNT7A expression and attenuates Wnt/β-catenin signaling, whereas MAZ binds to the WNT7A promoter and promotes its transcription. SMAD9 also associates with SMAD4, MAZ, and TOB1, accompanied by reduced MAZ occupancy at the WNT7A promoter. In addition, medroxyprogesterone acetate (MPA) increased SMAD9 expression and inhibited EC growth both in vitro and in xenograft models. MPA did not significantly alter SMAD9 promoter methylation using MethylTarget analysis, whereas PGR knockdown markedly attenuated the MPA-induced SMAD9 upregulation, suggesting that PGR signaling is required for MPA-induced SMAD9 expression. Together, these findings identify a DNMT3B-SMAD9-MAZ-WNT7A regulatory network linking epigenetic regulation of SMAD9 with transcriptional control of Wnt signaling in EC.

title: Deep learning-based multiomics integration identifies AI-defined tissue regions associated with cancer-associated fibroblast enrichment and chemoresistance in muscle-invasive bladder cancer.
abstract: Muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) frequently develops resistance to platinum-based chemotherapy, and tools for characterizing treatment-associated tumor microenvironmental features remain limited. We developed an artificial intelligence (AI)-based framework integrating pathological imaging, multiomics data, single-cell RNA sequencing, and ex vivo drug-sensitivity testing. Three convolutional neural network models trained using hematoxylin-and-eosin-stained whole-slide images from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) classified tumor, necrosis, and lymphocyte-enriched regions and were evaluated in an independent tissue microarray cohort. Patches negative for all three classifiers were designated AI-defined "Other" regions; this residual category was not trained as a cancer-associated fibroblast (CAF) classifier. Higher Other% was associated with shorter overall survival in univariable analyses, but the association was not significant after multivariable adjustment in TCGA. Multiomics and tissue-origin analyses linked Other% to stromal content. Scissor analysis of eight single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets identified Other-associated Scissor+ cells across epithelial and fibroblast compartments, while ACTA2 expression and extracellular matrix-remodeling pathways were enriched. In 48 MIBC specimens assessed by the hydrogel-embedded histoculture drug sensitivity test, Other% was higher in the gemcitabine-cisplatin-resistant group. Multiplex immunofluorescence further showed enrichment of alpha-smooth muscle actin signal in AI-defined Other regions. Erdafitinib showed ex vivo activity in a subset of specimens, but FGFR alteration status was unavailable and clinical efficacy was not evaluated. These findings support an association between AI-defined Other regions, CAF-related stromal features, and chemoresistance, while prospective validation is required before clinical use.

title: Genetic Prioritization of BTN3A2 Reveals an Interferon-Responsive T-Cell Program in Dermatomyositis Through Single-Cell Mendelian Randomization and Multi-Omics Integration.
abstract: Dermatomyositis (DM) is a complex autoimmune disorder characterized by genetic susceptibility and dysregulated immune activation. However, the relationship between genetic variation and specific immune cell states remains poorly understood. We aimed to identify genetically supported immune-cell-specific molecular programs underlying DM and investigate their biological relevance. We integrated immune-cell-specific single-cell expression quantitative trait loci (sc-eQTLs) from the OneK1K cohort with DM genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics using two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR). Candidate genes were replicated using an independent sc-eQTL dataset and prioritized by Bayesian colocalization. Multi-tissue validation was performed using skeletal muscle transcriptomics, peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC), and skin single-cell RNA sequencing, protein expression data, clinical phenotypes, virtual knockout analysis, and gain-of-function analyses of BTN3A2. We identified 204 immune cell-specific eGenes associated with DM and prioritized four high-confidence genes, including HLA-DRB1, HLA-C, Lnc-HLA-B-2, and BTN3A2. BTN3A2 showed robust colocalization across multiple CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell subsets and was further supported by muscle transcriptomic data. BTN3A2 was consistently upregulated in both DM muscle tissues and PBMCs and was broadly expressed across T-cell, NK-cell, and B-cell populations. BTN3A2+ T cells exhibited enhanced cytotoxic, activation, antigen-presentation, and interferon-responsive programs, which were reproduced in circulating PBMCs and lesional skin T cells. BTN3A2 expression was negatively correlated with MMT8 scores, while in silico knockout analysis implicated interferon-stimulated and antiviral pathways. Integrating cell-type-specific genetic evidence with multi-tissue immune profiling identified BTN3A2 as a genetically supported candidate associated with DM and an interferon-responsive T-cell state, providing novel insights for future mechanistic investigation.

title: VSMC DDR1 Mechanosensation Aggravates Atherosclerosis via Paracrine Signaling.
abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) increases cardiovascular risk and is linked to arterial stiffening and atherosclerosis. How stiffness promotes atherogenesis remains unclear. DDR1 (discoidin domain receptor 1), a mechanosensory tyrosine kinase receptor, has been implicated in force-regulated arterial remodeling. We investigated whether DDR1-mediated mechanosensation links arterial stiffness to vascular smooth muscle cell (SMC)-endothelial paracrine communication in CKD-related atherosclerosis. Single-cell RNA sequencing, secretome proteomics, and bulk RNA sequencing were integrated with stiffness-controlled models, endothelial assays, and a CKD-hyperlipidemia mouse model. SMC-specific Ddr1 deletion and a DDR1 dephosphorylation-targeting chimera (DEPTAC) were evaluated in vivo. Plasma TSP-1 (thrombospondin-1) levels were quantified in a CKD clinical cohort and analyzed in relation to renal function and atherosclerosis severity. CKD-associated vascular stiffening coincided with SMC phenotypic switching and enhanced THBS signaling. Multiomics integration identified THBS1 as a stiffness-induced SMC secretory effector. Stiff matrices increased SMC THBS1 secretion, promoting endothelial proliferation, migration, and leukocyte adhesion; these effects were attenuated by THBS1 knockdown. DDR1 coupled matrix stiffness cues to THBS1 expression by regulating its transcription via a tyrosine 3-monooxygenase/tryptophan 5-monooxygenase activation protein epsilon-FOXO3 (forkhead box O3) axis. Vascular SMC-specific Ddr1 deletion reduced aortic THBS1 levels, vascular stiffening, and atherosclerotic burden. DEPTAC suppressed aberrant DDR1 phosphorylation, reduced THBS1, and ameliorated vascular stiffening and atherosclerosis. Plasma THBS1 increased with CKD severity and correlated with atherosclerosis. DDR1-dependent mechanosensing in SMCs drives stiffness-induced paracrine signaling to endothelium via THBS1, promoting CKD-accelerated atherosclerosis. Targeting mechanical DDR1 activation may be therapeutic.

title: A novel LARP7 variant expands the phenotypic spectrum of Alazami syndrome and reveals transcriptomic dysregulation of developmental and extracellular matrix pathways.
abstract: LARP7 encodes a critical scaffold protein of the 7SK small nuclear ribonucleoprotein (7SK snRNP) complex that regulates RNA polymerase II transcriptional elongation. Biallelic loss-of-function variants in LARP7 cause Alazami syndrome, a rare neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by intellectual disability, growth restriction, and distinctive craniofacial features. However, the transcriptomic consequences of LARP7 deficiency in human cells remain poorly understood, and the phenotypic spectrum of the disorder is incompletely defined. We investigated a 6-year-old boy with clinically diagnosed Alazami syndrome who carried a novel homozygous LARP7 frameshift variant. Clinical evaluation and exome sequencing of blood-derived genomic DNA were performed, while quantitative PCR, Western blotting, and transcriptomic analysis were conducted using patient-derived dermal fibroblasts. Transcriptomic consequences of LARP7 deficiency were assessed by RNA sequencing, followed by single-subject differential expression, pathway enrichment, and network analyses. The patient presented with classical features of Alazami syndrome and tetralogy of Fallot, a cardiac manifestation not previously reported in the disorder. The novel homozygous LARP7 frameshift variant resulted in marked depletion of LARP7 transcripts and complete loss of full-length protein. Transcriptome-wide analysis identified 1,224 dysregulated genes involved in extracellular matrix organization, developmental remodeling, cell-cycle regulation, and immune signaling. Pathway and network analyses highlighted dysregulation of STAT3-associated signaling together with SMAD3-linked extracellular matrix and developmental programs, identifying candidate developmental and tissue-remodeling pathways that warrant further investigation in disease-relevant models. This study provides the first comprehensive transcriptomic characterization of genetically confirmed LARP7 deficiency in primary human cells and potentially expands the phenotypic spectrum of Alazami syndrome. The findings reveal widespread dysregulation of developmental and extracellular matrix pathways, offering new insight into the molecular basis of the multisystem manifestations of Alazami syndrome and providing a framework for future functional and genotype-phenotype studies.

title: BKPyVN-associated macrophage subpopulations and diagnostic biomarker identification - combine machine learning with single-cell analysis.
abstract: As pivotal effector cells of innate immunity, macrophages may play a critical role in immune regulation and fibrotic remodeling in BK polyomavirus nephropathy (BKPyVN) following kidney transplantation. However, their subpopulation heterogeneity, molecular characteristics, and functional mechanisms remain poorly understood. We integrated single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data from BKPyVN and stable transplant kidney (STK) biopsies. Pseudotime trajectory, CellChat, and high-dimensional weighted gene co-expression network analysis (hdWGCNA) were used to characterize BKPyVN-associated macrophages (BKPyVN-Mac) and identify related gene modules. Characteristic genes from these modules were used to construct diagnostic models from an integrated renal allograft microarray dataset, and nine machine-learning algorithms were compared. Key genes were validated by RT-qPCR and immunohistochemistry in human biopsies and by time-course transcript and protein analyses in a persistent mouse polyomavirus (MPyV) infection model. BKPyVN-Mac occupied a disease-associated macrophage state and may serve as a central communication hub within the allograft microenvironment. The support vector machine model exhibited the best diagnostic performance, with the highest area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC = 0.923). ATF4 and MCL1 were identified as key feature genes, and their upregulation was confirmed in human BKPyVN biopsies and, through their mouse orthologs Atf4 and Mcl1, in the persistent MPyV infection model. Functional analysis suggested that these genes are associated with inflammation, fibrotic remodeling, and metabolic regulation. This study characterizes the molecular phenotype and regulatory network of a BKPyVN-Mac subpopulation, providing new insights into BKPyVN pathophysiology and identifying candidate biomarkers for clinical diagnosis.

title: Integrated transcriptomic and functional analyses identify LAIR1 as a key immunoregulatory molecule in postoperative sepsis.
abstract: Postoperative sepsis arises from a dysregulated host response to infection following surgical stress. Current non-specific biomarkers offer insufficient predictive value, highlighting the need to identify molecular signatures that may facilitate earlier recognition of postoperative sepsis while providing insight into the underlying immune regulatory mechanisms. Transcriptomic datasets comprising postoperative septic and non-septic surgical cohorts, together with independent cohorts of sepsis and non-infectious systemic inflammation, were analyzed using Weighted Gene Co-expression Network Analysis and machine-learning approaches to identify hub genes. A diagnostic nomogram was constructed and validated across independent cohorts. A murine postoperative endotoxemia model (tibial fracture surgery followed by LPS challenge) was used for in vivo validation. Single-cell RNA sequencing analysis and LAIR1 antibody blockade were performed to assess cellular and functional relevance. A four-gene signature comprising LAIR1, PLAC8, ACSS2, and PCOLCE2 was identified. The resulting model achieved AUCs of 0.865 in GSE131761, 0.965 in GSE74224, 0.827 in E-MTAB-1548, 0.929 in GSE65682, and 0.997 in GSE77167. Among the four genes, LAIR1 showed the most sustained upregulation in peripheral blood and multiple organs during postoperative endotoxemia. Single-cell analysis identified monocytes as the predominant circulating source of LAIR1. LAIR1 blockade increased systemic cytokine release, aggravated multiorgan injury, and reduced survival. The four-gene signature reproducibly distinguished sepsis from infection-negative systemic inflammation across surgical and broader ICU cohorts. LAIR1 exhibited monocyte-enriched expression and a protective immunoregulatory role in postoperative endotoxemia, supporting its relevance to immune dysregulation of sepsis.

title: HDAC3 inhibition alleviates neuroinflammation and white matter injury after subarachnoid hemorrhage through modulation of BDNF/TrkB/NF-κB signaling.
abstract: White matter injury (WMI) is a major contributor to neurological deficits after subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH). Histone deacetylase 3 (HDAC3) is an established modulator of inflammatory responses, yet its contribution to post-SAH white matter pathology remains poorly understood. We used a rat endovascular perforation model and treated animals with RGFP966, a selective HDAC3 inhibitor. Clinical data, single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and transmission electron microscopy were integrated to evaluate cellular remodeling and structural integrity. Short- and long-term neurological recovery was assessed using a systematic battery of behavioral tests, while the underlying BDNF/TrkB/NF-κB signaling axis was validated through gain- and loss-of-function experiments. HDAC3 levels were elevated in both the CSF of SAH patients and rat brain tissues, inversely correlating with myelin basic protein (MBP) expression. RGFP966 treatment effectively preserved WMI, evidenced by reduced axonal injury and improved myelin shielding, and translated to superior long-term cognitive performance. ScRNA-seq analysis identified a profound shift in the microglial and oligodendrocyte-lineage landscapes after SAH. HDAC3 inhibition effectively curbed the expansion of pro-inflammatory microglial subsets while restoring homeostatic signatures and enhancing pro-myelination programs. Mechanistically, RGFP966 upregulated BDNF expression and restored TrkB phosphorylation, thereby suppressing NF-κB-mediated neuroinflammation. Notably, BDNF knockdown abolished the protective effects of HDAC3 inhibition, whereas exogenous BDNF mimicked the anti-inflammatory and myelin-protective phenotype induced by RGFP966. In conclusion, our findings demonstrate that HDAC3 is a pivotal driver of post-SAH neuroinflammation and WMI. Inhibition of HDAC3 exerts neuroprotection by recalibrating the microglial immune microenvironment and restoring the BDNF/TrkB axis.

title: Acrolein target-linked toxicological perturbation and tumor-immune microenvironment heterogeneity in colorectal cancer.
abstract: Acrolein is a highly reactive aldehyde generated endogenously during lipid peroxidation and encountered through environmental and dietary exposures. Although acrolein has established electrophilic, genotoxic, and oxidative-stress effects, the extent to which acrolein-linked gene perturbation is represented in colorectal cancer (CRC) transcriptomes and relates to tumor immune-stromal heterogeneity remains incompletely characterized. We integrated direct human acrolein target evidence from the Comparative Toxicogenomics Database (CTD) with TCGA-COAD/READ bulk RNA-sequencing profiles and a single-cell RNA-sequencing subset from GSE231559. The CTD curation yielded 179 unique direct human targets. Bulk analyses included 624 primary-tumor and 51 solid-tissue normal profiles. Single-cell analyses included six tumor and three normal libraries, yielding 24,128 retained cells assigned to eight broad marker-supported compartments. Target dysregulation burden, immune-stromal expression programs, and library-aware single-cell target localization were evaluated as transcriptomic summaries. In addition, RT-qPCR was performed in HCT 116 colorectal carcinoma cells to experimentally evaluate four measurable CTD targets (NFKBIA, GSTP1, VIM, and GPX4) after acrolein exposure. The bulk tumor-normal analysis identified 5,594 differentially expressed genes at FDR < 0.05 and |log2 fold change| ≥ 1. Of 179 CTD acrolein targets, 155 were measurable in the bulk dataset and 43 met the differential-expression threshold. Mean absolute normal-reference target burden was higher in tumors than normal tissue (1.96 vs. 0.75; difference 1.21; Welch p = 3.62e-42). Within primary tumors, target burden correlated negatively with T-cell and endothelial programs (rho = -0.27 for each), myeloid (rho = -0.20), fibroblast-ECM (rho = -0.19), and antigen-presentation programs (rho = -0.20), and positively with cell cycle (rho = 0.20). In single-cell data, descriptive mean target scores were highest in myeloid cells (0.455), fibroblasts (0.424), and endothelial cells (0.344). Cross-scale effects for 154 shared targets showed modest concordance (rho = 0.31, p = 6.95e-05). RT-qPCR showed vehicle-normalized relative expression of 2.18 ± 0.14 for NFKBIA, 1.83 ± 0.13 for GSTP1, 1.57 ± 0.15 for VIM, and 0.71 ± 0.09 for GPX4 after acrolein exposure (mean ± SD of three biological replicates). Acrolein target-linked expression perturbation is detectable in CRC and is associated with immune-stromal heterogeneity across bulk and single-cell transcriptomic scales. RT-qPCR provides targeted experimental support for acrolein-responsive expression changes in NFKBIA, GSTP1, VIM, and GPX4 in HCT 116 cells. These findings support a toxicogenomic framework for hypothesis generation but do not measure acrolein exposure in patients, establish causal toxicological effects in human tumors, or demonstrate a specific intercellular signaling mechanism. Additional mechanistic, protein/adduct, dose-response, and independent-cohort validation will be required to determine the biological significance of the observed associations.

title: Immune-programmed cell death crosstalk implicates plasma sTNFR1 as a candidate biomarker for sepsis-associated encephalopathy.
abstract: Sepsis-associated encephalopathy (SAE) is a frequent neurological manifestation of sepsis characterized by acute and diffuse brain dysfunction. Despite increasing evidence of molecular alterations in the septic brain, clinically applicable circulating biomarkers for SAE remain limited. Immune dysregulation and programmed cell death (PCD) pathways have been implicated in SAE pathogenesis, but their translational relevance for peripheral biomarker development remains unclear. This study aimed to identify immune-PCD crosstalk-related biomarkers for SAE through an integrated transcriptomic and clinical evaluation strategy. Human brain transcriptomic data from GSE135838 were analyzed using differential expression analysis and gene set enrichment analysis. Immune-related pathways, PCD signatures, and extracellular protein annotations were integrated to prioritize candidate biomarkers with peripheral detection potential. An exploratory cross-species comparison was performed using mouse SAE microglial RNA-sequencing data (GSE198862). Plasma soluble TNFR1 (sTNFR1) was subsequently evaluated in a prospective cohort of 60 septic patients (26 SAE and 34 non-SAE). SAE was defined as acute diffuse cerebral dysfunction during sepsis, identified by reduced GCS and/or a positive CAM-ICU assessment after exclusion of alternative causes, including persistent deep sedation that precluded reliable neurological assessment. Plasma samples for sTNFR1 measurement were collected within 24 h after enrollment, while SAE status was determined during the baseline neurological assessment after ICU admission. Logistic regression, ROC analysis, and bootstrap validation assessed the incremental value of sTNFR1, with 28-day mortality examined exploratorily. Transcriptomic analysis revealed activation of immune inflammatory responses and multiple PCD-related pathways in SAE brain tissue. Integration of immune, PCD, and differential expression signatures identified 15 immune-PCD crosstalk genes. Extracellular prioritization further identified FAS, IL6, and TNFRSF1A as candidate biomarkers. The immune-PCD signature showed substantial directional concordance in mouse SAE microglial transcriptomes, including concordant increases in Fas and Tnfrsf1a. In the clinical cohort, plasma sTNFR1 levels were significantly elevated in SAE patients compared with non-SAE patients (p < 0.001). After adjustment for age and SOFA score, sTNFR1 remained independently associated with SAE. Adding sTNFR1 increased the observed AUC from 0.791 to 0.891; however, the difference did not reach statistical significance by the paired DeLong test (p = 0.086). Continuous NRI nevertheless indicated improved reclassification (NRI = 0.950, 95% CI 0.411-1.536; p = 0.001). Exploratory analyses also associated SAE and higher sTNFR1 levels with increased 28-day mortality. This study integrates sepsis-associated brain transcriptomic discovery with prospective peripheral clinical evaluation and identifies circulating sTNFR1 as a candidate biomarker associated with SAE. sTNFR1 may provide additional information beyond conventional severity assessment for SAE identification and merits further validation.

title: Identification of ageing-related genes in prostate cancer with type 2 Diabetes using machine learning: a multi-omics study focusing on SOX4, PRNP, and FOXO4.
abstract: Prostate cancer (PCa) demonstrates complex associations with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and ageing, though their interconnected molecular mechanisms remain poorly defined. This study aimed to identify and validate diagnostic biomarkers at the intersection of these pathways to enable early detection and risk stratification in high-risk populations. Bioinformatic analysis was performed on PCa and T2DM transcriptomic data downloaded from the GEO database, followed by differential expression analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), and functional enrichment. Eight machine learning algorithms were applied to identify hub ageing-related genes (ARGs), with SHAP analysis interpreting feature importance. A nomogram model was constructed and validated across multiple cohorts. Immune infiltration, drug sensitivity, single-cell RNA sequencing, and spatial transcriptomics were used for mechanistic exploration. Three key ARGs (SOX4, PRNP, and FOXO4) were identified and used to develop a diagnostic model with high accuracy (AUCs: 0.726-0.905). SOX4 promoted immune evasion, PRNP exhibited context-dependent duality, and FOXO4 functioned as a tumor suppressor. Spatial and single-cell analyses revealed cell-type-specific expression and fibroblast-epithelial communication via MIF, LRP1, and FZD1. Drug sensitivity profiling identified abiraterone and docetaxel as potential therapeutics for high- and low-risk patients, respectively. In conclusion, SOX4, PRNP, and FOXO4 are key biomarkers linking PCa, T2DM, and ageing, and the diagnostic model shows robust performance and clinical utility, providing insights into microenvironment-driven mechanisms and personalized treatment strategies for PCa patients with T2DM.

title: An AI-derived inflammation-metabolism ecosystem signature reveals ATP2A2 as a microenvironment-remodeling driver of immune evasion in lung adenocarcinoma.
abstract: Chronic inflammation and metabolic dysregulation are increasingly recognized as interconnected drivers of tumorigenesis and immune evasion, yet their combined prognostic and mechanistic relevance in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains poorly defined. A curated 117-gene set representing systemic inflammation-metabolism dysregulation was obtained from MSigDB. Core prognostic genes were identified through differential expression analysis and univariate Cox regression. Using TCGA-LUAD as the training cohort and six independent GEO cohorts for external validation, 101 machine learning algorithm combinations were systematically evaluated to construct a robust prognostic model. Model performance was assessed by C-index, time-dependent ROC, and PCA. Immune characteristics were analyzed using TCIA, ESTIMATE, and TIMER-based deconvolution. ATP2A2, identified as the gene most strongly correlated with risk score, underwent multi-cohort transcriptomic and immunohistochemical validation, in vitro functional characterization, and mechanistic investigation via IOBR-integrated immune profiling. Single-cell RNA sequencing and multiplex immunofluorescence provided cellular-resolution verification of microenvironmental associations. The RSF + SuperPC model achieved optimal performance and effectively stratified patients into high- and low-risk groups with significantly divergent survival across all seven cohorts. High-risk tumors showed reduced immune/stromal infiltration and elevated tumor purity. ATP2A2 was consistently overexpressed in tumor tissue, correlated with poor differentiation, advanced stage, and shorter survival, and predicted immunotherapy resistance. Mechanistically, high ATP2A2 expression was associated with suppressed immune cell infiltration, attenuated chemokine signaling, impaired cancer-immunity cycle activity, and an "immune-desert" phenotype confirmed by single-cell and spatial analyses. This study establishes a validated inflammation-metabolism-based prognostic signature in LUAD and identifies ATP2A2 as a key driver linking tumor aggressiveness to immunosuppressive microenvironment remodeling, positioning it as a promising prognostic biomarker and potential therapeutic target for overcoming immunotherapy resistance.
